cmsFacts: CMS says only physicians and non-physician practitioners who are eligible to bill evaluation and management services can bill remote monitoring, and that auxiliary personnel can provide it under the general supervision of the billing practitioner.
CMS says only 1 practitioner can bill remote monitoring per patient in a 30-day period, and that remote physiologic monitoring and remote therapeutic monitoring cannot be billed together.
CMS says patient consent is required at the time RPM services are provided.
CMS says the 2 to 15 or 16 plus day data-collection requirement does not apply to the treatment management codes 98980, 98981, 99457 and 99458.

CMS says the device must meet the FDA definition of a medical device, and the data must be collected electronically and uploaded automatically to a secure location the billing practitioner can use for analysis.
metaDescription: CPT 99458 explained: the RPM add-on for each additional 20 minutes of management time. Pairing with 99457, documentation and billing limits.
summary: An add-on reported with 99457 for each additional 20 minutes of management time in the same month.
time: Each additional 20 minutes beyond the first 20
performer: Clinical staff under direction, or the practitioner

Time log showing minutes beyond the first 20
Notes showing the added time was interactive management

faqs.question: Is 99458 a separate stand-alone service?
faqs.answer: No. It only attaches to 99457 for the same patient and month.

faqs.question: What changed for short management time in 2026?
faqs.answer: A newer code, 99470, covers the first 10 minutes and cannot be billed with 99457. Check current rules to see which code fits each patient's month.
